claim: The Stocks-in-Play paper's universe is ~7,000 NYSE+Nasdaq stocks, Jan 2016-Dec 2023, explicitly free of survivorship bias (delisted names included, e.g. Twitter, delisted 2022-10-27), sourced from CRSP with IQFeed intraday data that is explicitly left unadjusted for splits/dividends.
quote: For instance, Twitter, which was delisted on October 27, 2022, is included in our database.
impact_on_spec: Local minute archive was populated from a current-active-asset snapshot (scripts/fetch_sip_universe.py load_universe() pulls only ACTIVE tradable assets); our own data-feasibility check found no minute-bar counterpart to the daily-only data/sip-delisted archive, so matching this survivorship-bias-free claim on our own minute data is an open, disclosed gap, not yet resolved.
limitations: Author-reported methodology description, not an independently re-run backtest of this exact universe; PDF text extraction, page-break/footnote splicing means only short contiguous spans are quoted verbatim.
independent_replication: QuantConnect's replication (orb_qc) confirms the general mechanism but explicitly narrows to the 1,000 most liquid names rather than testing survivorship-free coverage of the full ~7,000-name universe.

claim: Base eligibility (both Base and Stocks-in-Play variants): opening price above $5, 14-day average volume at least 1,000,000 shares/day, 14-day ATR more than $0.50. Stocks-in-Play adds: Relative Volume at least 100%, trade only the top 20 stocks by Relative Volume.
quote: The average trading volume over the previous 14 days had to be at least 1,000,000 shares per day.
impact_on_spec: Pins SIP01's eligibility filters exactly (price>$5, 14d avg vol>=1,000,000 sh/day, 14d ATR>$0.50, relvol>=100%, top-20-by-relvol); SIP02 preregisters a deliberately stricter version of the same four filters as a disclosed departure.
limitations: Filters as described in the paper's Base Strategy and Section 4; exact ATR look-back convention (Wilder vs simple 14-day true-range average) not fully disambiguated in the extracted text.
independent_replication: QuantConnect's replication uses the same $5 price and $0.50 ATR filters but substitutes 'top 1,000 by dollar volume' for the paper's $1M share-volume floor -- a disclosed discrepancy, see orb_qc_universe_and_replication_scope.

claim: Entry is a stop order (not a stop-loss order) placed at the high/low of the 5-minute opening range in the direction of that range's own move; a doji (open equals close in the first 5 minutes) places no order; protective stop is 10% of the 14-day ATR from the executed entry price; if not stopped, the position is closed at the end of the session (4:00pm ET). No profit target is described for the individual-stock Stocks-in-Play strategy.
quote: we placed a stop order (not to be confused with a stop loss order) at a level equal to the high/low of the 5-minute range, in the direction of the opening range
impact_on_spec: Confirms entry is a STOP order at the range extreme (matching this project's H-20260918-02 ETF proxy), but that script's added 10R profit target is NOT part of this paper's individual-stock rule -- SIP01/SIP02/SIP03 drop the target and exit only on stop or EOD, a disclosed correction versus the ETF proxy script.
limitations: The doji rule is stated as exact open==close; our own ETF proxy script instead used a |close-open|<=5%*(high-low) approximation -- SIP01-03 preregister the paper's exact rule, a disclosed departure from the ETF proxy's convention.
independent_replication: QuantConnect's C# implementation places a StopMarketOrder at OpeningBar.High/Low, matching the stop-order (not walk-in) entry type; no explicit doji handling visible in the excerpted code.

claim: Position size is set so a stop-out loses 1% of the capital deployed to that position; the paper caps leverage at 4x, citing FINRA pattern-day-trader margin rules for most US brokers.
quote: we imposed a maximum leverage constraint of 4x
impact_on_spec: SIP01/SIP02 preregister a house leverage_cap of 1.0x (no margin) as a disclosed, deliberate departure from the paper's 4x, for pattern-day-trader/margin-safety reasons pending an explicit broker-authorization decision; SIP03 (long-short diagnostic only) uses the paper's own 4x to attempt like-for-like fidelity.
limitations: 'Capital deployed for that position' is not spelled out as a per-slot fraction in the paper's own text; the QuantConnect replication code makes the equal-split convention explicit (risk 1% of TotalPortfolioValue/MaxPositions per slot, capped at equal-weight per name) and is used to resolve the ambiguity -- see orb_qc_universe_and_replication_scope.
independent_replication: QuantConnect's PlaceTrade sizing formula (stopLossRiskSize * TotalPortfolioValue / MaxPositions / (entryPrice - stopPrice), capped at a 1/MaxPositions equal-weight ceiling) is consistent with a 1%-of-equal-split-capital reading of the paper's rule.

claim: 2016-2023, long+short combined, top-20-by-relative-volume portfolio: total return 1,637%, annualized (IRR) 41.6%, Sharpe 2.81, max drawdown 12%, hit ratio 48.4%, annualized alpha 35.8%, beta 0.00, net of a $0.0035/share commission. The Base variant (same filters, no relative-volume/top-20 layer) returns only 29% total / 3.2% annualized / Sharpe 0.48 / MDD 13% over the same window; S&P 500 buy-and-hold returns 198% total / 14.2% annualized / Sharpe 0.78 / MDD 34%. No long-only or short-only breakdown is reported anywhere in the paper.
quote: A portfolio that consisted of the top 20 Stocks in Play achieved a total net performance of over 1,600%, with a Sharpe ratio of 2.81, and an annualized alpha of 36%.
impact_on_spec: Because the 2.81 Sharpe headline is a combined long+short number and no long-only split is published, SIP01/SIP02 (long-only) are NOT expected to reproduce 2.81; SIP03 (long-short diagnostic) is the only candidate positioned to sanity-check implementation fidelity against the published magnitude, and is explicitly excluded from promotion per this iteration's design constraints.
limitations: Author-reported backtest, MATLAB, zero independent audit of the full multi-year multi-thousand-stock run found; no bid-ask spread/market-impact term is mentioned in the extracted text beyond the flat per-share commission.
independent_replication: QuantConnect's replication reproduces the mechanism's *shape* (beats buy-and-hold, near-zero beta) on a single year (2016) and a narrower 1,000-name universe, not the full 2016-2023/7,000-name headline number.

claim: QuantConnect's independent replication narrows the universe to the 1,000 most liquid US equities above $5/share with ATR>$0.50 (versus the paper's ~7,000-name, $1M-share-volume-floor universe), backtests only 2016 (the first year of the paper's window), and reports a 2.396 Sharpe versus a 0.836 Sharpe SPY buy-and-hold benchmark over that single year, with -0.042 beta.
quote: The universe consists of the 1,000 most liquid US Equities that are trading above $5/share and have an Average True Range (ATR) > $0.50.
impact_on_spec: The registry's own caveat ('QuantConnect's headline ~2.4 Sharpe comes from a SINGLE year on the top-1000-liquid subset, not multi-year OOS') is confirmed verbatim; this iteration's design/select/2026 windows are all multi-year and the full local universe (subject to the survivorship caveat), not a single-year top-1000 replay.
limitations: QuantConnect's own parameter-sweep (5-25min range x 500-1500 universe size) found 17/25 (68%) combinations beat the benchmark, and an ATR-sensitivity sweep found all tested values beat it too -- the platform post does not claim this as robust multi-year OOS evidence, only as a single-year sensitivity check.
independent_replication: This is itself the independent replication of the primary paper; it is one party, not cross-checked against a second independent replication of the same code.

claim: A QuantConnect forum commenter (Yuri Lopukhov) identified that in minute-resolution backtests the protective stop order is only placed on the bar AFTER the entry stop order fills, so an entry filled at 9:35:01 gets its live-trading stop placed immediately but the backtest's stop is not placed until 9:36:00 -- a one-bar-late discrepancy between backtest and live/real-time execution. A separate commenter (AleNoc) reported Alpaca paper trading rejecting some of this strategy's stop orders as a 'wash trade'.
quote: entry order may be filled at 9:35:01, and in real-time stop order will be placed at that time, while in backtesting it will be placed at 9:36:00
impact_on_spec: Directly satisfies this task's requirement for a one-bar-late fill variant: every candidate's minute-bar simulation reports both the conservative same-bar stop-fill convention and a one-bar-late variant as a sensitivity check, per this exact community-reported discrepancy. The Alpaca wash-trade rejection is recorded as a live-feasibility risk for the future paper-trading step, not something this dossier resolves.
limitations: Forum comments, not a verified/audited report; unverified whether the wash-trade rejection is Alpaca-specific policy, an account-tier limitation, or a QuantConnect broker-adapter bug; this project has not independently reproduced either claim.
independent_replication: Not independently reproduced by this project; recorded as an unverified but concrete, named, dated community report, consistent with this repo's convention of keeping forum-sourced flags distinct from verified/audited claims.

claim: The same author group's 2026-07-08 study of the plain single-ETF (SPY) 5-minute ORB over Jan 2008-Dec 2025 found that, in its plain-vanilla form, the strategy fails to generate meaningful net-of-fee returns; simple economically-motivated filters, trade management and position-sizing enhancements raised CAGR from 1.0% to 12.1% and Sharpe from 0.14 to 0.84, but the detailed enhanced rules are paywalled and were not read. No 2024-25 update specific to the individual-stock Stocks-in-Play version was found in this pass.
quote: the strategy fails to generate meaningful net-of-fee returns
impact_on_spec: Corroborates, from the original authors themselves and as recently as 2026-07, that the single-ETF simplification (already refuted locally as dir:orb_etf_opening_range_breakout) is genuinely weak without the Stocks-in-Play selection layer -- consistent with, not contrary to, the local refutation; this iteration does not reopen the ETF direction and does not claim the individual-stock mechanism has any fresher-than-2024 published evidence than what was already in the registry.
limitations: Paywalled beyond the abstract/preview; the specific 'enhancements' are unknown and not assumed to be the same as this iteration's relative-volume/top-20 selection layer, even though both raise a weak base ORB toward profitability.
independent_replication: Author's own follow-up work, not an independent party; treated as recency context, not as confirmation of the Stocks-in-Play mechanism itself.
